raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# What does this PR do ?

`save_hf_pretrained` (and `save_hf_pretrained_modelopt`) now copy the source checkpoint's tokenizer and processor files instead of re-serializing them with `save_pretrained`.

Under transformers 5, re-serializing changes these files. Exporting Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (and Qwen3.5-0.8B) gave, compared with the source:

- `tokenizer.json` with different content (`pre_tokenizer`, `decoder`, `model`), and `tokenizer_config.json` without `added_tokens_decoder`;
- `preprocessor_config.json` switched from `Qwen2VLImageProcessorFast` to the slow `Qwen2VLImageProcessor`, plus a new `processor_config.json`;
- no `vocab.json`, `merges.txt` or `video_preprocessor_config.json`.

ModelOpt's Megatron exporter copies these files unchanged, so this also makes the bridge export match it (found while comparing the two on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B).

# Changelog

- `PreTrainedBase.save_artifacts` copies the source's files for each tokenizer / processor artifact that was loaded from the source and is unchanged since, instead of calling `save_pretrained` on it. The copied files include the tokenizer's own `vocab_files_names` and named chat templates (`additional_chat_templates/*.jinja`), at their relative paths. Hub sources (pinned revision, offline cache) go through the existing `_copy_custom_modeling_files`.
- Edits are detected from a cheap snapshot taken when the lazy property loads the artifact:
  - tokenizer: token count, added tokens, special tokens, chat template, padding / truncation side, `model_max_length`, and a fast tokenizer's normalizer, pre-tokenizer, post-processor and decoder;
  - processor: its config, chat template and tokenizer.
- These artifacts are still saved with `save_pretrained`:
  - one assigned to the wrapper (`model.tokenizer = ...`);
  - one edited in place (`add_special_tokens`, `pad_token = ...`, a new `chat_template`, a backend normalizer, ...);
  - one loaded with arguments that change it (`model_max_length`, `padding_side`, `subfolder`, ...). Only download / model-loading arguments (`revision`, `cache_dir`, `token`, `torch_dtype`, `device_map`, ...) keep the copy;
  - one whose source has none of its files.

  Their saved files win over another artifact's source copies.
- Docs: `docs/bridge-guide.md` notes the copy and when it falls back to `save_pretrained`.

One visible difference: `PreTrainedCausalLM` sets `pad_token = eos_token` when the source tokenizer has none; that change was saved before and now isn't, so the export's tokenizer matches the source.

# Tests

- New unit tests in `tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py`:
  - unchanged source artifacts are copied and not re-serialized;
  - a replaced processor's saved files win over the tokenizer's source copies;
  - an artifact the source has no files for is still saved;
  - with a real `PreTrainedCausalLM` tokenizer: unedited or only used for encoding, it is copied verbatim; after `add_special_tokens`, a new `chat_template`, a backend normalizer edit, a load-time `model_max_length` override or the setter, it is re-serialized and keeps the change. The two in-place edit cases fail on the first commit of this PR, and the normalizer and load-argument cases on its second;
  - named chat templates are copied and reload under their names (fails on the second commit).
- `tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained`, `test_auto_bridge.py`, `training/test_checkpointing.py`: 957 passed, 1 skipped (`nvcr.io/nvidian/nemo:26.10.rc9`).
- `PreTrainedCausalLM("Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B").save_artifacts(...)` against the source snapshot: before, 3 files missing, 1 extra and 4 differing; now only `config.json` differs. With an edited chat template, the tokenizer files are re-saved and the processor files still match the source.

# Before your PR is "Ready for review"

**Pre checks**:

- [x] Make sure you read and followed [Contributor guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Did you write any new necessary tests?
- [x] Did you add or update any necessary documentation?
- [ ] Does the PR affect components that are optional to install? (Ex: Numba, Pynini, Apex etc)
  - [ ] Reviewer: Does the PR have correct import guards for all optional libraries?

# Additional Information

- Related to #4804

Right now save_artifacts still calls save_pretrained on every artifact first. Then _copy_source_artifact_files overwrites those files with

Ideally we need to remember where each artifact came from when it is loaded, and also take a cheap snapshot of it (for example `len(tokenizer)`, the added tokens and the special tokens). This might be overkill.. just flagging it here

- tokenizer: token count, added tokens, special tokens, chat template, padding / truncation side, `model_max_length`;

[P2] Preserve explicit tokenizer load-time overrides

**Failure:** Save a local tokenizer with `model_max_length=128`, construct `PreTrainedMaskedLM(source_dir, model_max_length=256)`, then call `save_artifacts(target)`. The [loader forwards the override](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/src/megatron/bridge/models/hf_pretrained/masked_lm.py#L155-L163), but this snapshot records the already-overridden tokenizer. The subsequent fingerprint therefore matches, and export copies the source configuration containing 128 rather than saving the effective value 256. Explicit `padding_side` overrides are similarly lost. The previous unconditional serialization preserved these arguments.

**Correction:** Update `_load_artifact` / `_copies_source_files` to distinguish explicit serialization-affecting load overrides from unchanged source state. Compare effective overrides against source configuration, or conservatively serialize the affected artifact when such overrides are supplied. The invariant is that explicit user configuration survives export. The complete per-artifact override set is not established by the inspected source, so a generic allowlist patch would be speculative.

**Preservation:** Ordinary source loads must remain byte-for-byte copies; `revision` and cache-selection arguments must not alone force serialization. Preserve causal-LM's intentional internal `pad_token = eos_token` copy behavior, while retaining explicit pad-token overrides, post-load edits, and setter replacements.

**Acceptance — proposed, not executed:** Using the tiny local-tokenizer setup in [the new regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py#L826-L854), save a maximum length of 128, load the masked-LM wrapper with 256, export, and assert `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(target).model_max_length == 256`. Repeat with source `padding_side='right'` overridden to `'left'`. Without overrides, assert source-byte equality and no serialization. Retain all four existing tokenizer-edit cases.

[P2] Include persisted fast-tokenizer backend edits in the fingerprint

**Failure:** This tuple omits the backend model, normalizer, pre-tokenizer, post-processor, and decoder. Using the two-token WordLevel source from [the new test](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py#L834-L837), load it through `PreTrainedMaskedLM` and assign `wrapper.tokenizer.backend_tokenizer.normalizer = tokenizers.normalizers.Lowercase()`. Every fingerprint field remains unchanged, so export copies the old `tokenizer.json` and loses the edit. Before export, `encode('A', add_special_tokens=False)` returns `[0]`; after reloading the export, it returns the unknown-token ID `[1]`. Previously, serialization preserved the normalizer.

**Correction:** Extend `_artifact_fingerprint` to include persisted fast-tokenizer backend components. Do not simply compare the entire `backend_tokenizer.to_str()` without normalization: normal encoding can change transient padding/truncation settings. The invariant is that changed persisted tokenization behavior triggers serialization, while ordinary encoding does not. The exact normalized representation needs verification against supported dependency versions, so no unverified generic patch is proposed.

**Preservation:** Unchanged fast tokenizers must still copy source bytes before and after encoding. Slow tokenizers must not require backend attributes. Retain added/special-token, chat-template, setter-replacement, and causal-LM internal pad-token behavior.

**Acceptance — proposed, not executed:** Apply `Lowercase()` as above, export, reload, and assert `encode('A', add_special_tokens=False) == [0]` and that the saved backend contains the lowercase normalizer. In unchanged counterparts, including one that performs padded/truncated encoding before export, assert source-byte equality and no serialization. Retain all cases of [the existing edit regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py#L826-L854), and check a slow tokenizer remains eligible for copying.

[P2] Preserve named chat-template files when copying artifacts

**Failure:** A tokenizer saved with `chat_template = {'default': '...', 'tool_use': '...'}` has a named template under `chat_templates/tool_use.jinja`. Neither the tokenizer nor processor patterns include that directory. Other tokenizer files match, so the [fallback serialization](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/src/megatron/bridge/models/hf_pretrained/base.py#L327-L346) does not run. An unchanged export therefore loses `tool_use`, and selecting that template after reload no longer reproduces the source. The previous `save_pretrained` path retained named templates.

**Correction:** Include `chat_templates/*.jinja` for tokenizer and processor artifacts and preserve their relative paths through staging and final copying. Adding the pattern alone is insufficient: both the [local helper](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/src/megatron/bridge/models/hf_pretrained/base.py#L240-L248) and final artifact copy flatten paths. Create destination parents and make write tracking recursive and relative-path-aware so serialized nested templates retain precedence. Whether to extend the shared helper's path contract or use an artifact-specific copy path needs care; the required invariant is that each source template remains addressable by its original name.

**Preservation / acceptance — proposed, not executed:** Extend [the real-tokenizer setup](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py#L826-L854) with `default` and `tool_use` templates. Export unchanged and assert both template files are byte-identical, both mapping keys survive reload, and rendering each name matches the source. Cover local and mocked Hub/offline-cache sources. Retain root `chat_template.jinja` copying and the existing replacement-processor assertion that its saved template wins; add the equivalent precedence assertion for a serialized nested template.

detail.body:
# What does this PR do ?

`save_hf_pretrained` (and `save_hf_pretrained_modelopt`) now copy the source checkpoint's tokenizer and processor files instead of re-serializing them with `save_pretrained`.

Under transformers 5, re-serializing changes these files. Exporting Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (and Qwen3.5-0.8B) gave, compared with the source:

- `tokenizer.json` with different content (`pre_tokenizer`, `decoder`, `model`), and `tokenizer_config.json` without `added_tokens_decoder`;
- `preprocessor_config.json` switched from `Qwen2VLImageProcessorFast` to the slow `Qwen2VLImageProcessor`, plus a new `processor_config.json`;
- no `vocab.json`, `merges.txt` or `video_preprocessor_config.json`.

ModelOpt's Megatron exporter copies these files unchanged, so this also makes the bridge export match it (found while comparing the two on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B).

# Changelog

- `PreTrainedBase.save_artifacts` copies the source's files for each tokenizer / processor artifact that was loaded from the source and is unchanged since, instead of calling `save_pretrained` on it. The copied files include the tokenizer's own `vocab_files_names` and named chat templates (`additional_chat_templates/*.jinja`), at their relative paths. Hub sources (pinned revision, offline cache) go through the existing `_copy_custom_modeling_files`.
- Edits are detected from a cheap snapshot taken when the lazy property loads the artifact:
  - tokenizer: token count, added tokens, special tokens, chat template, padding / truncation side, `model_max_length`, and a fast tokenizer's normalizer, pre-tokenizer, post-processor and decoder;
  - processor: its config, chat template and tokenizer.
- These artifacts are still saved with `save_pretrained`:
  - one assigned to the wrapper (`model.tokenizer = ...`);
  - one edited in place (`add_special_tokens`, `pad_token = ...`, a new `chat_template`, a backend normalizer, ...);
  - one loaded with arguments that change it (`model_max_length`, `padding_side`, `subfolder`, ...). Only download / model-loading arguments (`revision`, `cache_dir`, `token`, `torch_dtype`, `device_map`, ...) keep the copy;
  - one whose source has none of its files.

  Their saved files win over another artifact's source copies.
- Docs: `docs/bridge-guide.md` notes the copy and when it falls back to `save_pretrained`.

One visible difference: `PreTrainedCausalLM` sets `pad_token = eos_token` when the source tokenizer has none; that change was saved before and now isn't, so the export's tokenizer matches the source.

# Tests

- New unit tests in `tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py`:
  - unchanged source artifacts are copied and not re-serialized;
  - a replaced processor's saved files win over the tokenizer's source copies;
  - an artifact the source has no files for is still saved;

The two in-place edit cases fail on the first commit of this PR, and the normalizer and load-argument cases on its second;
  - named chat templates are copied and reload under their names (fails on the second commit).

- `PreTrainedCausalLM("Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B").save_artifacts(...)` against the source snapshot: before, 3 files missing, 1 extra and 4 differing; now only `config.json` differs. With an edited chat template, the tokenizer files are re-saved and the processor files still match the source.

Right now an artifact only counts as "changed by the user" when it is set through the setter (`model.tokenizer = ...`). If someone edits the tokenizer in place, for example `tokenizer.add_special_tokens(...)`, `tokenizer.pad_token = ...` or a new `chat_template`, we still treat it as unchanged and copy the source files. The user's edits are lost without any warning. If they also resized the embedding, the exported vocab no longer matches the exported weights.

Ideally we need to remember where each artifact came from when it is loaded, and also take a cheap snapshot of it (for example `len(tokenizer)`, the added tokens and the special tokens). This might be overkill.. just flagging it here

Thanks, fixed in 1fba2d4ef. When a tokenizer or processor is loaded, we now record a cheap snapshot of it:
- tokenizer: token count, added tokens, special tokens, chat template, padding / truncation side, `model_max_length`;
- processor: its config, chat template and tokenizer.

At save time, an artifact that differs from its snapshot, or that was replaced, is saved with `save_pretrained`. So `add_special_tokens`, `pad_token = ...` or a new `chat_template` are kept. Only unedited artifacts get the source files. The setters no longer need to mark anything. New tests cover adding special tokens, a new chat template and replacing the tokenizer; the two in-place edit cases fail on the previous head.

[P2] Preserve explicit tokenizer load-time overrides

**Failure:** Save a local tokenizer with `model_max_length=128`, construct `PreTrainedMaskedLM(source_dir, model_max_length=256)`, then call `save_artifacts(target)`. The [loader forwards the override](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/src/megatron/bridge/models/hf_pretrained/masked_lm.py#L155-L163), but this snapshot records the already-overridden tokenizer. The subsequent fingerprint therefore matches, and export copies the source configuration containing 128 rather than saving the effective value 256. Explicit `padding_side` overrides are similarly lost. The previous unconditional serialization preserved these arguments.

**Correction:** Update `_load_artifact` / `_copies_source_files` to distinguish explicit serialization-affecting load overrides from unchanged source state. Compare effective overrides against source configuration, or conservatively serialize the affected artifact when such overrides are supplied. The invariant is that explicit user configuration survives export. The complete per-artifact override set is not established by the inspected source, so a generic allowlist patch would be speculative.

**Preservation:** Ordinary source loads must remain byte-for-byte copies; `revision` and cache-selection arguments must not alone force serialization. Preserve causal-LM's intentional internal `pad_token = eos_token` copy behavior, while retaining explicit pad-token overrides, post-load edits, and setter replacements.

**Acceptance — proposed, not executed:** Using the tiny local-tokenizer setup in [the new regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py#L826-L854), save a maximum length of 128, load the masked-LM wrapper with 256, export, and assert `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(target).model_max_length == 256`. Repeat with source `padding_side='right'` overridden to `'left'`. Without overrides, assert source-byte equality and no serialization. Retain all four existing tokenizer-edit cases.

Using the two-token WordLevel source from [the new test](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py#L834-L837), load it through `PreTrainedMaskedLM` and assign `wrapper.tokenizer.backend_tokenizer.normalizer = tokenizers.normalizers.Lowercase()`. Every fingerprint field remains unchanged, so export copies the old `tokenizer.json` and loses the edit. Before export, `encode('A', add_special_tokens=False)` returns `[0]`; after reloading the export, it returns the unknown-token ID `[1]`. Previously, serialization preserved the normalizer.

**Correction:** Extend `_artifact_fingerprint` to include persisted fast-tokenizer backend components. Do not simply compare the entire `backend_tokenizer.to_str()` without normalization: normal encoding can change transient padding/truncation settings. The invariant is that changed persisted tokenization behavior triggers serialization, while ordinary encoding does not. The exact normalized representation needs verification against supported dependency versions, so no unverified generic patch is proposed.

**Preservation:** Unchanged fast tokenizers must still copy source bytes before and after encoding. Slow tokenizers must not require backend attributes. Retain added/special-token, chat-template, setter-replacement, and causal-LM internal pad-token behavior.

**Acceptance — proposed, not executed:** Apply `Lowercase()` as above, export, reload, and assert `encode('A', add_special_tokens=False) == [0]` and that the saved backend contains the lowercase normalizer. In unchanged counterparts, including one that performs padded/truncated encoding before export, assert source-byte equality and no serialization. Retain all cases of [the existing edit regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py#L826-L854), and check a slow tokenizer remains eligible for copying.

[P2] Preserve named chat-template files when copying artifacts

**Failure:** A tokenizer saved with `chat_template = {'default': '...', 'tool_use': '...'}` has a named template under `chat_templates/tool_use.jinja`. Neither the tokenizer nor processor patterns include that directory. Other tokenizer files match, so the [fallback serialization](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/src/megatron/bridge/models/hf_pretrained/base.py#L327-L346) does not run. An unchanged export therefore loses `tool_use`, and selecting that template after reload no longer reproduces the source. The previous `save_pretrained` path retained named templates.

**Correction:** Include `chat_templates/*.jinja` for tokenizer and processor artifacts and preserve their relative paths through staging and final copying. Adding the pattern alone is insufficient: both the [local helper](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/src/megatron/bridge/models/hf_pretrained/base.py#L240-L248) and final artifact copy flatten paths. Create destination parents and make write tracking recursive and relative-path-aware so serialized nested templates retain precedence. Whether to extend the shared helper's path contract or use an artifact-specific copy path needs care; the required invariant is that each source template remains addressable by its original name.

**Preservation / acceptance — proposed, not executed:** Extend [the real-tokenizer setup](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/1fba2d4ef240a7f365a78a74268e4ef7d021dc2a/tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/test_base.py#L826-L854) with `default` and `tool_use` templates. Export unchanged and assert both template files are byte-identical, both mapping keys survive reload, and rendering each name matches the source. Cover local and mocked Hub/offline-cache sources. Retain root `chat_template.jinja` copying and the existing replacement-processor assertion that its saved template wins; add the equivalent precedence assertion for a serialized nested template.

reviews.body:
Right now save_artifacts still calls save_pretrained on every artifact first. Then _copy_source_artifact_files overwrites those files with
  the source's and deletes any leftovers. Does it make sense to make copying the default, and only fallback to reserialization if an artifact is changed or for some reason not in the source?

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=moderate -->

Three export correctness regressions need fixes: explicit tokenizer load overrides, persisted backend edits, and named chat templates can be silently lost.

Reviewed all six changed files and their directly affected export paths. The earlier added-token, single chat-template assignment, and wrapper-replacement cases now select serialization in the current source. The findings below cover distinct remaining failures. This was a static review; tests were not executed.
